answer: Continuous co-location proof. Each identity must periodically submit a delta between two ambient sensor readings taken from its claimed physical host, signed with a hardware key bound to that host. A verifier cross-checks the delta against neighboring readings, and the mismatch tolerance acts as a cipher only genuine co-located hosts can satisfy. Anyone faking identities must supply distinct physical hosts with real sensors, so the umber of forged identities is capped by hardware an operator can actually deploy and maintain.
